summary: A card with a status but no tokens no longer shows an empty token track (#1279, Mendon's ruling, all card types). CardTokenRail draws its hardware, takes the pointer and takes focus only when the card has public tokens. With no tokens the status track takes the inner position next to the card edge (upright or bowed), after any permanent-change seal, and WidthFor/Tracks reserve one track instead of two. A seal alone keeps one track's room with no empty hardware. Cards with tokens keep the existing two-track layout. New native probe StatusRailProbe + tools/check-status-rails.sh.
validation: Client builds with 0 warnings/0 errors. New check-status-rails passes at 1920x1080 and 1280x800: 13 status combinations (act, move, straighten, target, rule, contribute, protect each alone; all seven; all + seal; seal only; move+straighten+act; tokens+statuses; tokens only) x 11 in-play fixtures (Personality home/battlefield/bowed, Follower/Item/Spell attached, Bamboo Harvesters upright and bowed, Stronghold, Region, Ring), 151 rails, plus a native click on a status-only track selecting its card. Negative check: forcing the token track visible fails the probe on the first card. Screenshots inspected. Existing checks pass: token-rails, restriction-rails (incl. engine-driven table and expiry), permanent-grants, fallen, action-lock-ui, created-copies-ui, copy-ui (one flaky hover failure, passed on rerun and on main). check-stat-tokens fails identically on unchanged main (battle-tokens board never prints STAT_TOKEN_PASS); not caused by this change.
remaining: Mendon's hands-on look in a real game. Celestials are excluded from the client's status display (RestrictionRail.HasEffects omits Zone.Celestial), unchanged here. check-stat-tokens battle-tokens failure is pre-existing on main.
